of northwest North Carolina, including the following areas, Ashe and
Watauga.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Mohave, AZ; Clark, NV
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 245 PM PDT /245 PM MST/, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms
producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.5 and 1 inch
of rain has fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Searchlight, Cottonwood Cove Campground, Cottonwood Cove, Hoover
Dam, Cal-Nev-Ari, Temple Bar Campground, Willow Beach and Temple
Bar.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Henderson, NC
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive runoff continues.

* WHERE...Central Henderson County in western North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 600 AM EDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding around greater Hendersonville.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 535 PM EDT, Mud and Bat Fork Creeks remained in flood and
flooding will continue all afternoon.  The Mud Creek river gage
on North Main Street was nearing 16 feet which indicates flooding
of portions of William H King Memorial Park and the Oklawaha
Greenway.  The river has crested in Hendersonville, but will not
fall below flood stage until late evening or overnight tonight.

- Please obey all barricades and heed all evacuation orders from
local Emergency Management officials.  Only a few inches of water
can strand your vehicle and only 6 inches of water can sweep your
vehicle away.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Hendersonville, Fletcher, Flat Rock, Mountain Home, Laurel Park,
Valley Hill and East Flat Rock.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Martin, FL
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern Martin County in east central Florida...

* Until 700 PM EDT.

* At 523 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Stuart, Jupiter Island, Port Salerno, Hobe Sound, Palm City,
Sewall's Point, Witham Field, Hobe Sound Beach and Hobe Sound
Wildlife Refuge.
